claims.summary: Yang (2020) distinguishes subject, object, and listener honorification in Korean; the paper discusses -시- and listener-directed endings as separate resources within the honorification system.

The National Institute of Korean Language guide describes speech levels addressed to the listener and relates their choice to social factors such as age and position and to whether the situation is formal.

The entry’s proposed checklist separates the referent of honorific marking from listener-directed speech level and asks the learner to consider social relation and formality, reflecting the cited sources’ distinct categories and contextual factors.
